GEO600 in 2014: Towards a darker dark port

GEO600 overlaps two laser beams after they travelled (twice) through both of its 600 meter long arms. A little bit of laser light leaves the interferometer at its output port. It is used to measure the arm length differences (caused by gravitational waves). But some small amount of light caused by imperfections of the mirrors also shows up there.

In 2014, the GEO600 team installed a compensation system to lower the amount of the disturbing additional light: By heating one of the mirrors from the sides, the new system could match the radii of curvature of the mirrors. This reduced the amount of the unwanted extra light and improved the sensitivity of the detector.
